failures are never auto-fixed), and the merge gate in `pr_merge.py` — reads
those exact-head statuses and the manifest comment this script publishes
(`local/protocols/issues-prs.md` §2), and nothing else.

## 1. What it is

The parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull
request produces exactly **one** CI completion event, which the auto-fix
dispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one
invocation, one manifest, one exit code.

```
local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]
                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]
```

`<pr-id>` is the GitHub PR number; the script reads `branch`, `base` and the
head SHA from GitHub (`gh_common.py pr-view`), finds the branch's worktree (via
`git worktree list`, falling back to `.worktrees/<branch with / → ->`), and
runs everything **inside that worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary
checkout, and the worktree's branch tip must equal the remote head before the
run starts.

Exit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at
least one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start
(unknown PR number, missing worktree, unresolvable base, GitHub unreachable —
a GitHub error never degrades to a local record).

### Preconditions that are hard errors, never silent skips

| Precondition | Why it is fatal |
|---|---|
| GitHub returns an open PR with a head branch | there is no branch to test |
| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |
| `origin/<base>` or `<base>` resolves | invariant 8 — the diff-based audits and the change gating self-disable without a base, which is exactly the "checks silently stopped running" failure the parent repo patched twice |
| a merge base exists | the change set is undefined without one |
| `python3` on `PATH` | every audit job and the manifest writer need it |

There is deliberately **no `LOCAL_CI_ENABLED` kill switch**. `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`
and `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely
stops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green
light it never earned. If CI must not run, do not run it — the head SHA simply
keeps whatever statuses it already carries.

## 2. Job table

Eight steps, in this order, named exactly after the parent workflow's job ids
so the auto-fix dispatcher's mapping (build → ci-fix, blueprint-render →
blueprint-fix, everything else → never auto-fixed) ports without translation.

| Step | Parent job | What it runs (in the worktree) | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build` | `build` (`pr-ci.yml:115-168`) | warm `.lake/build`, `lake exe cache get`, `lake build`, `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit` (`:155-156`), `scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py` (`:158-159`) | `lean ∨ comparator ∨ workflow` |
| `blueprint-render` | `blueprint-render` (`:173-243`) | `leanblueprint pdf` + non-empty `blueprint/print/print.pdf` (`:210-218`), `texra-blueprint bbl` (`:222-223`), `texra-blueprint web` with `grep '^ERROR:'` (`:225-243`) | `blueprint_src ∨ workflow` |
| `paper-gaps` | `paper-gaps` (`:248-271`) | `texra-blueprint --root . paper-gaps check` | `paper_gaps ∨ workflow` |
| `blueprint-sync` | `blueprint-sync` (`:273-317`) | `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`, `blueprint_lean_sync.py --update-lean-decls`, `blueprint_lean_sync.py --ci`, `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py --base-ref` | `lean ∨ blueprint ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `file-length` | `file-length` (`:319-340`) | `check_oversized_lean_files.py --root .` (>1000 lines) | `mip_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `proof-debt` | `proof-debt` (`:342-386`) | `unittest test_audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py`, `audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py --ci` | `mip_lean ∨ tex_chapter ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `proof-evasion` | `proof-evasion` (`:388-445`) | four regression tests, then `audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py --ci`, `audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci`, `audit_unfaithful_markers.py --ci`, and `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py --ci` (advisory) | `mip_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `statement-origin` | `statement-origin` (`:447-487`) | `check_statement_paper_origin.py --root .` | `ldt_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |

Every step is blocking. The single advisory sub-check is
`check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`: exit 1 means "candidates reported" and is
downgraded to a warning, any other nonzero status is a real failure — the same
`set +e` dance as `pr-ci.yml:432-445`.

Two GitHub-only behaviours are dropped on purpose: `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`
blocks and `::error` / `::notice` / `::warning` annotations are inert outside
Actions, so the step's stdout+stderr log **is** the summary. `--github-annotations`
is not passed to `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`. Exit-code semantics are
preserved exactly: `::warning` never failed a job, and the `^ERROR:` grep
always did.

### Steps that did not run

A step whose area did not change is recorded `skipped` with the reason — never
omitted. A skipped step is green for the merge gate, exactly as a skipped
GitHub job is. This is why the gating globs are load-bearing (§3): a glob that
under-matches turns a real gate into a permanent, invisible `skipped`.

## 3. Gating globs — keep in lockstep

`git diff --name-only --no-renames <merge-base> <head>` replaces
`dorny/paths-filter@v3`. `--no-renames` is deliberate: reporting both the old
and the new path means a rename *out of* a gated tree still trips that tree's
filter, and deletions count. `*` in these patterns spans `/`, matching
minimatch's `**`.

| Area | Globs | Parent |
|---|---|---|
| `lean` | `*.lean`, `lakefile.*`, `lean-toolchain`, `lake-manifest.json` | `pr-ci.yml:84-88` |
| `mip_lean` | `MIPStarRE/*.lean` | `:89-90` |
| `ldt_lean` | `MIPStarRE/LDT/*.lean` | `:91-92` |
| `blueprint` | `blueprint/*` | `:93-94` |
| `blueprint_src` | `blueprint/src/*` | `:95-96` |
| `tex_chapter` | `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` | `:97-98` |
| `paper_gaps` | `docs/paper-gaps/*`, `texra-blueprint.toml`, `MIPStarRE/*.lean`, `blueprint/src/*`, `docs/*.md` | `:99-107` |
| `scripts` | `scripts/*` | `:108-109` |
| `comparator` | `scripts/comparator/*` | `:110-111` |
| `workflow` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml`, `local/bin/*`, `local/protocols/*`, `.githooks/*` | `:112-113`, extended |

> **Lockstep warning.** These globs must move together with the trees the audit
> scripts actually scan. The parent repo patched the `paper_gaps` filter twice
> after checks silently never ran — the note at `pr-ci.yml:102-104` is the scar.
> The failure mode is asymmetric: an over-broad glob costs CPU, an under-broad
> glob costs a merged regression that no check ever looked at. When you widen
> a scan tree in `scripts/*.py`, widen the matching glob in `ci.sh` in the same
> commit, per `meta.md` §5.

The `workflow` area is the one deliberate extension. On GitHub it meant "the
workflow file changed, so re-run everything"; locally the workflow layer is a
whole tree — the frozen reference `pr-ci.yml`, every driver and helper under
`local/bin/`, every protocol under `local/protocols/`, and the hooks in
`.githooks/` — and a change to any of them forces a full run, every step
included. The globs are that broad on purpose: a `gh_common.py`-only change has
to run the `scripts/tests` unit suite that covers it — carried by
`blueprint-sync` — and under the old three-file glob such a change matched no
area and ran nothing at all (PR 7 review, F13).

## 4. Manifest schema

Built in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then
posted as the manifest PR comment (§5):

```
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.json          complete run
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.partial.json  partial run
```

A run is **partial** when it was given `--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`;
`--dry-run` writes nothing at all.

Step logs live outside the repository, under
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.

```jsonc
{
  "schema": 1,
  "generator": "local/bin/ci.sh",
  "replaces": ".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml",
  "pr": 7,                       // GitHub PR number
  "branch": "issue-7-qpbt-basis",
  "base": "main",                // from the GitHub PR
  "base_ref": "origin/main",     // what actually resolved
  "merge_base": "<sha>",
  "head_sha": "<sha>",           // the SHA every step ran against
  "worktree": "/abs/path",
  "started": "2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800",   // ISO-8601 with offset
  "finished": "2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800",
  "seconds": 1125,               // whole run, integer
  "conclusion": "success",       // success | failure | error
  "partial": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict
  "areas": { "lean": true, "blueprint_src": false, ... },
  "changed_files": ["MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean", ...],
  "warnings": ["texra-blueprint not installed; skipped ...", ...],
  "steps": [
    {
      "step": "build",           // one of the eight job ids, always all eight
      "outcome": "success",      // success | failure | error | skipped
      "seconds": 883,
      "log_path": "/Users/…/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/0007/<sha>/build.log",
      "blocking": true,
      "note": ""                 // skip reason, exit code, or degradation cause
    }
  ]
}
```

Outcome vocabulary — the distinction is what routes the auto-fix loop:

| `outcome` | Meaning | Auto-fix |
|---|---|---|
| `success` | the step ran and passed | — |
| `failure` | the step ran and the code is wrong | `build` → ci-fix, `blueprint-render` → blueprint-fix, everything else → **never** |
| `error` | the step could not run (missing tool, unbootstrapped worktree, build lock unavailable) | never — this is an operator problem, not a code problem |
| `skipped` | gated out, or excluded by `--only` / `--skip-build` | — |

`conclusion` is `failure` if any step failed, else `error` if any step errored,
else `success`. The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == "success"`.

## 5. Publication

Evidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against
(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:

* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the
  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`
  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish
  "absent" from "not applicable";
* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;
* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked
  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.

`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,
killed or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the
review gate's "green CI on the same head SHA" check (invariant 2) fails closed.
Immediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch
tip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits
nonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.

A **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`) publishes nothing at
all — no statuses, no manifest comment — and keeps its manifest in runtime
storage only. `--base` belongs on that list because an overridden base (the PR
head, say) can empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success. Partial runs
are a debugging aid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and
they must not clobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.

## 6. Concurrency and locks

Two advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each
holds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its
owner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`
(default 3 h).

| Lock | Scope | On contention |
|---|---|---|
| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |
| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |

Only the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and
take nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and
take nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them
per-file without serializing.

`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs
(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —
the ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:
killing a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.
So a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is
waited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove
the lease directories by hand.

## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache

`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the
shared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save
policy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of
~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,
so no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a
worktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.

1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,
   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:
   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a
   hard error.
   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);
     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.
2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and
   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never
   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main
   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,
   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`
   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run
   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.
3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at
   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`. That bootstrap path is where the ProofWidgets
   prune workaround lives, and a package-free tree is exactly the state that
   triggers it. `MIPSTARRE_CI_ALLOW_COLD_FETCH=1` overrides for a tree you know
   is clean.
4. `lake build`, then `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`, then the
   comparator drift check.

Every `lake` and `python3` invocation goes through a subshell that unsets
`git rev-parse --local-env-vars` first. Inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`
make Lake resolve nested package repositories against the wrong repository;
`.githooks/pre-push:19-24` does the same thing for the same reason, and any
orchestrator that invokes `ci.sh` from inside a git hook inherits the problem.

Lake's staleness is trace-hash-based, not mtime-based, so a restored snapshot
older than the merge base is safe — but only within one
`hash(lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, lakefile.toml)` class. Crossing that
boundary is `build-cache.md`'s problem, not this protocol's: `ci.sh` delegates
the check to `warm-worktree.sh` and simply builds whatever it is handed.

## 8. The axiom audit is reported, not run

`blueprint-sync` deliberately has no Lean setup. On GitHub that was forced by
repeated runner disk exhaustion, and the job degraded to a `::notice` telling a
human to run the audit locally (`pr-ci.yml:303-317`). Locally the constraint is
different but the conclusion is the same: the machine has a single full-build
budget, already spent by `build`. So `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py` runs, and
when it answers `true` the run records a warning:

> run `python3 scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` in a Lean environment

De-automation of this kind is a legitimate evolution step (`meta.md` §4), and
this one is inherited rather than invented.

## 9. Telemetry

When `build` actually ran (any outcome but `skipped`), one line is appended to
`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`:

```json
{"ts":"…","kind":"ci-build","trigger":"ci.sh pr=0007","seconds":883,
 "outcome":"success","sha":"…","note":"branch issue-7-qpbt-basis"}
```

This satisfies the `meta.md` duty that every full build be accounted for, and
makes "how much wall time did CI cost this PR" answerable by a script. The
per-step seconds in the manifest are the finer-grained record.

## 10. Trust boundary

Two things about `ci.sh` are worth stating plainly.

**It executes branch-authored code.** The audit scripts, the test suite, and
`lakefile.toml` all come from the worktree under test, because that is what CI
means and what the parent workflow did. Never run `ci.sh` on a branch you would
not run a shell script from.

**Its logs are untrusted data.** Compiler diagnostics, plasTeX output and test
failures can contain arbitrary text, including text shaped like instructions.
`ci.sh` stores logs verbatim and makes no attempt to clean them. Any consumer
that feeds a log into an agent prompt — `autofix.sh` above all — owes the
sanitization required by invariant 6: strip control characters, break fences,
truncate, and frame the payload as data that must not be followed. The manifest
gives consumers `log_path` rather than log content precisely so this stays the
consumer's explicit, visible responsibility.

## 11. Deliberate deviations from the parent workflow

| Parent | Local | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `::error`/`::notice`/`::warning` | per-step log file + `warnings` array | inert outside Actions; exit codes carry all gating meaning |
| `cancel-in-progress` for PR runs | second run refused, running builds never killed | local build state is not disposable |
| cache `restore`/`save` actions | hot-main snapshot read via `warm-worktree.sh`; `ci.sh` never writes the shared cache | invariant 1 — the eviction failure documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142` |
| `workflow` filter = the YAML file | also `local/bin/ci.sh`, `local/protocols/ci.md` | the CI definition is now three files |
| `--github-annotations` on the duplicate-helper audit | dropped | annotation-only flag |
| `push`-to-main and docs-only `pull_request` triggers | none | the docs-only paths existed solely to emit the completion event that started PR Review (`pr-ci.yml:31-33`); locally the lifecycle script calls `review.sh` directly |
| implicit "PR event" job conditions | every run is a PR run | `ci.sh` is only ever invoked on a GitHub PR number |

## 12. Amendments

Changing a gating glob, a step's command set, the manifest schema, the status
contexts or their vocabulary, or a lock's name or semantics is an amendment:
record the trigger in `results/telemetry/events.md`, edit this file and
`ci.sh` together, append to `EVOLUTION.md`, and grep `local/` for every other
enforcement point (`meta.md` §5). The manifest schema in particular is a
contract with `review.sh`, `autofix.sh` and `pr_merge.py`; bump `schema` when
it changes incompatibly.

What is being replaced, and why it was built that way\n\nThe parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented\nfailure. weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *\"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget.\"* |\n| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *\"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache.\"* |\n| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *\"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile.\"* |\n| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |\n| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *\"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could valuable\ncache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the\nsame failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared\nbuild tree.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The two-tier split\n\n`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and\ndifferent sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the\nparent's failure.\n\nAn absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>` for a\none-component branch name. The helper rejects `/`, symlink targets, escape, and\ncanonical overlap with packages, `hot-main`, the repository, or any worktree,\nplus canonical-equal ownership by another worktree. Export it before setup or\nwarming and through dispatch and cleanup; only its target gets `--add-dir`.\n\n**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,\n`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the\nparent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and\ndistributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**\ncopy.\n\n**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The\nparent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud\ncache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Identity is by\n> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old\n> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches\n> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,\n> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. The cache key\n\n```\nkeyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )\n```\n\nconcatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local\nanalog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in\n`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`\nand `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay\nbyte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.\nA missing input file is a hard error, never a default.\n\nTwo properties matter, and they are not symmetric:\n\n1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's\n   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest\n   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is\n   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash\n   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not\n   need their timestamps preserved.\n2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,\n   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.\n   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`\n   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls\n   back to the cold path. Nothing in it is ever\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\n\n```\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\nstatus=complete|partial\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\nwarmer_version=1\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\n                          [--targets \"<lake targets>\"] [--lock-timeout S]\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\n```\n\n### 5.1 Writer lease\n\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\n\nStaleness is decided in this order:\n\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\n\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\nprevent.\n\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\n\n### 5.2 Build\n\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\n   finish, then warm again.\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\n   **No `lake update`.**\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\n   prompts may later read.\n\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\n\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\n\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\n\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\n\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\n\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\n\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\nso loudly.\n\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\"main did not build cleanly\"* —\nnot *\"nothing was published.\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\nreason to retry.\n\n### 5.5 Retention\n\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\n```\n\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\n\nDecision procedure:\n\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\n\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\n\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\n\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\n  clone;\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\n\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\n\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\n\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\n\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\n\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\nlocking there.\n\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\n\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\nwhat a stale lock is.\n\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\n\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\n\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \"no pid, therefore\n  stale\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\n  field is read as \"this host\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\n\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\n\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\n   error.\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\n   if the pin is not already installed.\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the\n   documented failure this check exists to surface.\n6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).\n7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the\n   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed\n   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.\n   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).\n   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the\n   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol\n   exists to prevent.\n8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`\n   calls out `--check` specifically for *\"each fresh worktree used for a PR.\"*\n\n`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero\nif anything is missing.\n\n### 8.1 Git environment hygiene\n\nEvery invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in\n`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every\nvariable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a\nscript invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into\nLake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.\n\n### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround\n\nKept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a\npristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.\n\n*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib\npost-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before\nfetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not\nexist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create\nthe directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.\n\n*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is\n**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.\nRecorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed\nby a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts\ntherefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before\nfetching.\n\n`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete\ndownloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks\na checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from\nsource.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\n\n```jsonc\n{\"ts\": \"<ISO 8601 with offset>\",\n \"kind\": \"warm\" | \"rebuild\" | \"cache-get\",\n \"trigger\": \"<who asked for this>\",\n \"outcome\": \"success\" | \"failed\",\n \"seconds\": <int>,\n \"sha\": \"<commit, when known>\",\n \"note\": \"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\"}\n```\n\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\n\nThree properties are load-bearing:\n\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\n  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.\n* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s\n  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every\n  failure path degrades to a warning.\n* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400\n  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is\n  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Operating procedures\n\n```bash\n# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main\n\n# What is published right now?\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status\n\n# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis\n\n# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check\n\n# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force\n\n# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status\n```\n\nAfter a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm\nfirst, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot\nis invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run\n`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in\neach worktree serialized behind one lock.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades\n\n| condition | behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |\n| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |\n| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |\n| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |\n| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |\n| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |\n| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |\n| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |\n| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |\n| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |\n| `origin/main` does not resolve | Warning, non-zero exit from `--check`, because hooks self-disable silently. |\n| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). Consumer: warning, telemetry skipped. |\n\n---\n\n## 12. Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\ncodebase.\n\n## Catalogue\n\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\n\n---\n\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\n\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\nan extra hypothesis. The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\nanywhere in Lean.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\n  directly.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\n\n```lean\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\n\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) :\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\n\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro α β\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\n  ...\n```\n\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\n\n---\n\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\n\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \"precondition not met.\" Downstream\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\nfunction. core.hooksPath=.githooks

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"
HOOK_ROOT="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS="$(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)"

run_without_git_local_env() (
  # Git exports repository-local variables while running hooks.  Several script
  # tests create temporary repositories; keep those tests independent of this
  # checkout.
  unset $GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS
  "$@"
)

# A merge commit can be syntactically valid while its index has been reset to
# the first-parent tree.  That failure mode silently discarded clean incoming
# additions on issue-109 and issue-110 (issue #222).  Check the pending index
# before every other gate, including the documented blanket hook bypass: a
# missing incoming path is valid only when the branch deleted a base path.
MERGE_HEAD_PATH="$(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking the merge result for silent incoming loss."
  python3 "$HOOK_ROOT/local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py" --repo "$ROOT"
fi

# Scope-control guard (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01, the issue-0007 overbuild):
# workflow scaffolding is budgeted at <=1000 changed lines per commit (400 until the owner raised it on 2026-09-05).  This is
# mechanical enforcement — repeated verbal correction of scaffolding bloat did
# not stick, so the budget lives in the hook.  The override env var is granted
# by the OWNER per commit, never self-granted by an agent session.  Runs
# before the ACMR early-exit so deletion-only commits are counted too
# (numstat includes deletions; PR 7 round 3, F8), and before the
# MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS exit so a blanket hook skip cannot launder the
# owner-only budget override.
# A merge that carries main stages already-reviewed content.  A merge head
# contained in github/main measures the budget against MERGE_HEAD; a merge head
# that contains github/main (a parent branch of a stack that already merged
# main; owner decision 2026-09-05) measures it against github/main, so inherited
# main content counts zero while the PR's cumulative workflow diff and any
# side-branch content beyond main still count.  Any other side-branch merge
# stays budgeted against HEAD.
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor MERGE_HEAD refs/remotes/github/main 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse MERGE_HEAD)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: main-history merge; budget measured against MERGE_HEAD."
elif [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/remotes/github/main MERGE_HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/github/main)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge carrying github/main; workflow-layer content beyond github/main is budgeted."
else
  BUDGET_BASE=""
  if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge; workflow-layer merge content is budgeted."
  fi
fi
INFRA_CHANGED="$(git diff --cached --numstat $BUDGET_BASE -- local/ .githooks/ \

ZERO_SHA="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"

usage() {

Usage: local/bin/checked-push.sh [--repo-root PATH] REMOTE LOCAL_REF:REMOTE_REF

Run .githooks/pre-push against one explicit branch ref, then push that ref.
Both refs must use their full refs/heads/... names.
EOF
}

die() {
  printf '%s: error: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2
  exit 2
}

  local checkout_sha checkout_state

Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\\n   prompts may later read.\\n\\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\\n\\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\\n\\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\\n\\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\\n\\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\\n\\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\\n\\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\\nso loudly.\\n\\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\\\"main did not build cleanly\\\"* —\\nnot *\\\"nothing was published.\\\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\\nreason to retry.\\n\\n### 5.5 Retention\\n\\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\\n\\n```\\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\\n```\\n\\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\\n\\nDecision procedure:\\n\\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\\n\\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\\n\\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\\n\\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\\n  clone;\\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\\n\\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\\n\\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\\n\\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\\n\\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\\n\\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\\nlocking there.\\n\\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\\n\\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\\nwhat a stale lock is.\\n\\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\\n\\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\\n\\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \\\"no pid, therefore\\n  stale\\\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\\n  field is read as \\\"this host\\\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\\n\\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\\n\\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\\n   error.\\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\\n   if the pin is not already installed.\\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the\\n   documented failure this check exists to surface.\\n6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).\\n7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the\\n   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed\\n   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.\\n   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).\\n   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the\\n   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol\\n   exists to prevent.\\n8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`\\n   calls out `--check` specifically for *\\\"each fresh worktree used for a PR.\\\"*\\n\\n`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero\\nif anything is missing.\\n\\n### 8.1 Git environment hygiene\\n\\nEvery invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in\\n`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every\\nvariable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a\\nscript invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into\\nLake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.\\n\\n### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround\\n\\nKept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a\\npristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.\\n\\n*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib\\npost-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before\\nfetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not\\nexist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create\\nthe directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.\\n\\n*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is\\n**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.\\nRecorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed\\nby a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts\\ntherefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before\\nfetching.\\n\\n`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete\\ndownloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks\\na checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from\\nsource.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 9. Telemetry\\n\\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\\n\\n```jsonc\\n{\\\"ts\\\": \\\"<ISO 8601 with offset>\\\",\\n \\\"kind\\\": \\\"warm\\\" | \\\"rebuild\\\" | \\\"cache-get\\\",\\n \\\"trigger\\\": \\\"<who asked for this>\\\",\\n \\\"outcome\\\": \\\"success\\\" | \\\"failed\\\",\\n \\\"seconds\\\": <int>,\\n \\\"sha\\\": \\\"<commit, when known>\\\",\\n \\\"note\\\": \\\"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\\\"}\\n```\\n\\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\\n\\nThree properties are load-bearing:\\n\\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\\n  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.\\n* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s\\n  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every\\n  failure path degrades to a warning.\\n* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400\\n  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is\\n  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 10. Operating procedures\\n\\n```bash\\n# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).\\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main\\n\\n# What is published right now?\\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status\\n\\n# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.\\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis\\n\\n# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.\\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check\\n\\n# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.\\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force\\n\\n# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?\\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status\\n```\\n\\nAfter a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm\\nfirst, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot\\nis invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run\\n`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in\\neach worktree serialized behind one lock.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades\\n\\n| condition | behaviour |\\n|---|---|\\n| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |\\n| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |\\n| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |\\n| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |\\n| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |\\n| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |\\n| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |\\n| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |\\n| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |\\n| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |\\n| `origin/main` does not resolve | Warning, non-zero exit from `--check`, because hooks self-disable silently. |\\n| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). /-!
# Combining the point measurements

This module proves the construction of the joint X/Z point measurements
and defines their scalar linear coarse-graining.  The latter is
the genuine postprocessing of a complete measurement on each heterogeneous
player space.

## References

The construction is `lem:qld-4-10` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, with paper source
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709`.
The coarse-graining is `lem:qld-4-12` in the same blueprint, with paper source
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:993-1011`.
-/

/-- A pair of source points and the two scalar coefficients used by the
extended point measurement. -/
abbrev ExtendedPointQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) :=

    (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P)

namespace CombinedPointsWitness

/-- Coarse-grain a joint point measurement by `(a,b) |-> alpha*a + beta*b`
on the selected player side.  This is the concrete measurement of
`lem:qld-4-12`, paper lines 993--1011. -/
noncomputable def extendedQ {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δ : ℝ}
    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ)
    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)
    (alpha beta : PauliScalar P) :
    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
  (points.Q side x z).postprocess fun ab => alpha * ab.1 + beta * ab.2

end CombinedPointsWitness

Operational acceptance requires a natural post-merge completion whose coordinator-owned
batch shows `ready_at` before completion, the actual activation call before detailed
adoption, and the successor's current `task_started` and first useful output. That one
transition establishes ordering, not sustained floor coverage; the existing interval audit
remains the latter's evidence.
Children do not write the primary index or shared telemetry concurrently. The primary
telemetry owner records each child using `telemetry.py native-record ROLLOUT` with
`--name --role --issue --thread-id --root-thread-id --key-label --worktree --status`
and `--job-class --requested-model`, plus `--hardness-reason` for hard Astra jobs.
Effective bound-turn contexts must satisfy the recorded classification. Root/parent IDs,
timestamps, outcome and raw observed counters are retained. Aggregation scope is
unknown: never sum parent and child counters without independent evidence. Native
review uses the exact-head transport in `review.md`; it cannot bypass CI or merge gates.
The root's inherited permission envelope is unchanged; reviewers receive read-only
assignments, not a falsely claimed separate read-only sandbox. Historical episodes,
attempt counts and usage survive refreshes and route changes without a budget reset.

## 2. Roles and sandboxes

### Sol-first jobs (superseding owner amendment, 2026-09-07)

Issue #301 comment5573256033 supersedes the earlier cleanup-only whitelist.
Routine/bounded jobs default to exact `gpt-5.6-sol`/`ultra`, including routine
existing-statement proof work, build repairs and independent reviews. Main chooses
`--job-class hard|escalated|source_semantic|control_policy|hard_review` with an
explicit `--hardness-reason` for genuinely difficult or escalated Astra work.
New game/hypothesis/source-semantic decisions and control-policy reviews justify
Astra; Lean files, prover/reviewer roles, or missing historical samples alone do not.
Exact edit specifications remain appropriate for mechanical cleanup, not a universal
Sol gate. The historical C01/C02 audit is retained as evidence, not a role ceiling.

For a model change create a NEW explicit-model native child with Ultra and
`fork_turns="none"`; follow-up to an Astra thread does not switch its model.
Link predecessor thread, assignment, worktree, checkpoint and cumulative budget.
No permission, account, root identity, lease or capacity setting changes here.
All current-turn contexts are checked; observed models are not inferred from a
requested argument. Independent review still binds identity, fresh assignment,
head, prompt and actual completed turn. Hard control-policy review remains Astra.

At reviewed activation, main records one timestamp and passes `--activation-at`
to native telemetry (or `MIPSTARRE_MODEL_POLICY_ACTIVATION_AT` to the publisher).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
r"""Report-only audit for conclusion-shaped theorem hypotheses (anti-pattern A1).

Issue #493 documents a proof-evasion pattern where a theorem replaces a named
bridge-package input by an inline existential whose body is essentially the
same as the theorem conclusion.  This script is a deliberately conservative
heuristic for the inline-existential case:

* parse Lean ``theorem`` / ``lemma`` headers;
* compare each explicit hypothesis containing an existential against the
  theorem conclusion;
* report hypotheses whose salient tokens overlap enough to deserve human
  review.

The tool is **report-only** by default.  With ``--ci`` it exits non-zero only
for unapproved review findings; witness-adapter declarations with names such as
``fooOfWitness`` are still printed but treated as allowed helper adapters.  The
heuristic is not a Lean parser and should not be used to prove absence of all
A1 variants; it is a reviewer tripwire for the PR #491-style mutation.
"""

        return tuple(f for f in self.findings if f.allowed_helper)

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.LowDegreeGameTheorems
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.PauliBasisTest

/-!
# Polynomial combination and restricted line distributions

This file contains the concrete definitions at the foundation of the
Chapter 15 combining argument.  A pair of bounded individual-degree
polynomials is embedded into the two coordinate blocks of an extended
polynomial.  On lines, explicit affine reparameterizations are composed with
coefficient-list polynomials.  The original-dimensional restricted line laws
are formed before decoding, while their field seed is still present.

## References

The combining map is blueprint
`def:combine-map`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`.
The restricted laws are blueprint `def:ith-restricted-line`,
with paper origin in the same source at lines 1038--1048.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

noncomputable section

/-- The bounded individual-degree polynomial outcome used by the global
pair measurement.  This is the actual `polyFunc` subtype from
`def:polyfunc`, not a coefficient-box replacement. -/
noncomputable abbrev Poly (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
  ↥(MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (PauliScalar P) P.d)

/-- Pairs of bounded polynomial representatives returned by the global
measurement in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
noncomputable abbrev PolyPair (P : AdmissibleParams) := Poly P × Poly P

/-- Split the extended coordinate set into the `X` block, the `Z` block, and
the two scalar coordinates.  This is formalization-only coordinate plumbing
for blueprint
`def:combine-map`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
def finCombineEquiv (m : ℕ) :
    Fin (2 * m + 2) ≃ ((Fin m ⊕ Fin m) ⊕ Fin 2) :=
  (finCongr (by omega)).trans
    (finSumFinEquiv.symm.trans
      (Equiv.sumCongr finSumFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl (Fin 2))))

/-- Embed an `X`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
def embX (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
  fun i => (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inl i))

/-- Embed a `Z`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
def embZ (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
  fun i => (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inr i))

/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `alpha`. -/
def alphaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
  (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 0)

/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `beta`. -/
def betaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
  (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 1)

/-- Project an extended point onto its `X` coordinate block. -/
def projX {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
  fun i => u (embX m i)

/-- Project an extended point onto its `Z` coordinate block. -/
def projZ {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
  fun i => u (embZ m i)

/-- Combine two multivariate polynomials by the formula
`alpha * f(x) + beta * g(z)` from `def:combine-map`.

Blueprint `def:combine-map`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-983`. -/
noncomputable def combinePoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ}
    (f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * m + 2)) K :=
  MvPolynomial.X (alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.rename (embX m) f +
    MvPolynomial.X (betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.rename (embZ m) g

/-- Evaluation of `combinePoly` is the displayed combining formula. -/
theorem combinePoly_eval {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ}
    (f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    MvPolynomial.eval u (combinePoly f g) =
      u (alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (projX u) f +
        u (betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (projZ u) g := by
  change MvPolynomial.eval u (combinePoly f g) =
    u (alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (u ∘ embX m) f +
      u (betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (u ∘ embZ m) g
  simp [combinePoly, MvPolynomial.eval_rename]

/-- Evaluate one member of a global polynomial pair at a point, selecting the
component by Pauli basis.  This is formalization-only support for
`lem:qld-4-7`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1274`. -/
def evalAt {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (pair : PolyPair P) : PauliScalar P :=
  match W with
  | .X => MvPolynomial.eval u pair.1.1
  | .Z => MvPolynomial.eval u pair.2.1

/-- Interpret a bounded coefficient list as an ordinary univariate
polynomial.  This helper makes the line-combination definition use Mathlib's
actual polynomial composition operation. -/
noncomputable def linePolynomialOfCoefficients {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
  ∑ i : Fin (c + 1), Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val

/-- Evaluating the polynomial represented by a coefficient list agrees with
`evalCoefficient`. -/
theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) (t : K) :
    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).eval t = evalCoefficient f t := by
  change Polynomial.eval t
      (∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val) =
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, f i * t ^ i.val
  rw [Polynomial.eval_finsetSum]
  simp

/-- The univariate polynomial before coefficient extraction in
`combineLinePoly`.  The four first scalars describe the affine parameters on
the two projected lines; the last four are the affine `alpha` and `beta`
coordinates of the extended line. -/
noncomputable def combineLinePolynomial {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c : ℕ}
    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K)
    (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
  (Polynomial.C uα + Polynomial.C vα * Polynomial.X) *
      (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).comp

    (Polynomial.C uβ + Polynomial.C vβ * Polynomial.X) *
      (linePolynomialOfCoefficients g).comp
        (Polynomial.C aZ + Polynomial.C bZ * Polynomial.X)

/-- The seed event defining the `i`-th original-dimensional restricted line
law.  It is applied before the `LineDesc` decoder, since a geometric line does
not determine the retained seed. -/
def restrictedLineSeedEvent (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m)
    (sample : LdSpace L × LdSpace L) : Prop :=
  chiIndex L sample.1.seed = i

/-- Decidability of the pre-decoding seed event. -/
instance restrictedLineSeedEvent_decidablePred (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
    DecidablePred (restrictedLineSeedEvent L i) := by
  intro sample
  unfold restrictedLineSeedEvent
  infer_instance

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary for `def:ith-restricted-line`: whenever a line
CL map keeps the shared scalar coordinate, the pre-decoding law it generates
